Therefore, when it is said that Joseph should go and see the peace of his brethren, the advent of Himself is signified; every advent is said to occur when truth flows into the thought from the Word.

4713. *And the peace of the flock*, that this signifies how it is with those who are learning, or the Church, is evident from the signification of peace, which is how one fares, concerning which just above in n. 4712; and from the signification of the flock, which are those who are learning, for a shepherd, or one who feeds, is he who teaches and leads to the good of charity, and the flock is that which learns and is led, concerning which in n. 343, thus also the Church.

4714. *And bring me back word*, that this signifies knowledge, is evident from the signification of bringing back word, which is to report how a matter stands, thus knowledge.

4715. *And he sent him from the valley of Hebron*, that this signifies from the Divine Natural and Sensual, is evident from the signification of being sent, which is to proceed and teach, concerning which above in n. 4710; from the signification of a valley, which are those things that are below, concerning which in n. 1723, 3417; and from the signification of Hebron, which is the Church of the Lord regarding good, concerning which in n. 2909. Thus, through those words it is signified that He would teach those things that are the lower things of the Church, and this is because they could not grasp the higher things; for whoever teaches faith and not charity can never perceive the higher or inner things of the Church, for he has nothing that leads him, and that dictates whether this pertains to faith or whether this is true. But if he teaches charity, then he has good; this is a dictate to him, and it leads him, for every truth is from good and deals with good, or, what is the same, everything of faith is from charity and deals with charity. That everything of doctrine should look to life, anyone can know from natural light alone. That by those words it is signified from the Divine Natural and Sensual, is the higher sense; for those things which are the lower things of the Church are said to be from the Divine Natural and Sensual of the Lord, not that these things are lower in the Lord, for in the Lord and in His Divine Human everything is Infinite, for He is Jehovah regarding both Essences, n. 2156, 2329, 2921, 3023; but because it is so with man. For those who are sensual men grasp those things that are in the Lord and from the Lord sensually, and those who are natural grasp them naturally; it is thus said according to the quality of those who receive. But those who are celestial men, and from that state are truly rational, they perceive the inner things; concerning them it is said that they are taught from the Divine Rational of the Lord. This is the higher sense, as has been said, which is signified by those words. That a valley represents the lower things of the Church can be evident from other passages in the Word, such as in Isaiah: “*The prophecy of the valley of vision; what is to thee here, that thou hast gone up all to the roofs: a day of tumult, and of trampling, and of perplexity, to the Lord Jehovih Zebaoth, in the Valley of vision*,” XXII: 1, 5; the valley of vision stands for fantasies about spiritual things from sensual things, thus from lower things. In the same: “*The choice of thy valleys were filled with chariot, and the horsemen have set themselves at the gate*,” XXII: 7; the choice of valleys stands for goods and truths in the natural or external man. In the same: “*The voice of one crying in the desert, prepare the way of Jehovah, make level in the solitude a path for our God, every valley shall be exalted*,” XL: 3, 4; a valley stands for the humble.
